refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: Spacecraft value copies preserve the complete captured covariance, including estimated correlations. The configured OrbitErrorCovariance and sigma fields retain their own captured values. Copying a spacecraft does not rebuild its estimated covariance from those prior settings; editing those settings still applies their normal prior updates.

A Spacecraft resource is GMAT's spacecraft model and includes data and models for the spacecraft's orbit, epoch, attitude, and physical parameters (such as mass and drag coefficient), as well as attached hardware, including tanks and thrusters. The Spacecraft model also contains the data that configures how the Spacecraft 3-D CAD model is used in an OrbitView. Spacecraft has certain fields that can be set in the Mission Sequence and some that cannot. See the field tables on the pages below for more information.

OrbitParameterAccess = Native (default) retains writable RMAG and SemilatusRectum calculation parameters. Set OrbitParameterAccess = Worksheet before the mission sequence to make these two derived calculation parameters read-only for this spacecraft, as specified in the legacy NASA worksheet. Reads and all other parameter access rules are unchanged. EA, MA and HA support writes in both modes subject to their conic-domain restrictions. This setting is saved with the spacecraft, follows spacecraft clones and function scope, and is available in the Qt resource editor's Orbit section. It cannot be changed by a mission command. State inputs in the spacecraft's selected display representation remain available for defining its orbit.

Estimation restoration applies saved values within the spacecraft's existing attitude, propulsion, power, hardware and plate components. Saved values require compatible component and state layouts; changes to those declarations require preparing a new run.
